hero.title: Every replay you have played, read together
hero.tagline: Import your Pokémon Showdown replays and see which of your teams is winning, which four you brought, and where your score went. Every number says how many games it came from.

import.title: Import in one go
import.body: Paste replay links, or sync every public replay a Showdown name has played.

teams.title: Teams and brings, added up
teams.body: Battles with the same six are counted together, then the four you brought in each of them, and teams are ranked on win rate and how many games they have.

timeline.title: Read a replay as text and images
timeline.body: Open any game and the battle is laid out as text and images. Watching a replay on Showdown runs the animation, which is comparatively heavy; this way you can step through it turn by turn to review.

start.title: Getting started
start.one: Signing in with Google is the only way in.
start.two: Add the Showdown names you play under, and each battle is matched to whichever side carries one of them.
start.three: Paste a few replay links, or sync a whole account and leave it running.
start.note: Showdown gives no other site a way to confirm that an account is yours, so a name by itself grants nothing. It only decides which of the battles you imported count as your own.
start.cta: Sign in and import your first replay

about.title: About
about.lede: Blueberry Academy reads the replay links you give it. This page says what it reads, how it counts, and what it leaves out, so that when you see a win rate you know where it came from.

source.title: What it reads
source.body: One Showdown replay is one game. The raw record is fetched from replay.pokemonshowdown.com and stored exactly as it arrived. Everything else is worked out from it: the format, the result, the six revealed at team preview, the four that appeared. Nothing is typed in by hand. If more of a record can be read later, the rest is worked out again from the copy already stored, not fetched a second time.

counting.title: How battles are counted
counting.unit: Every game is stored on its own, including the games of a Bo3 series. A series result can be worked out from its games, and not the other way round. Bo1 counts games, Bo3 counts series.
counting.format: Bo1 and Bo3 should be treated as two entirely different things. The same team can perform very differently under each, so they are counted separately.
counting.spectated: A battle where neither player is on your list of Showdown names counts as a spectated battle. It is stored and you can read it, but it counts towards none of your statistics.

teams.title: Teams and brings
teams.team: A team is the six revealed at the pick screen. Two battles are the same team as long as the six Pokémon and the format match; items, moves and EV spreads are no part of that, because not every battle makes them public.
teams.bring: A bring is the four that actually appeared. In a game that ends early the fourth may never show up, which happens often. Those games count for the team but for none of the brings, and the team page explains when that is what you are looking at.

ranking.title: How team performance is ranked
ranking.body: Ranking uses a cautious win rate rather than the raw one. Three wins from three games is a 100% win rate, but on that few games it sits below a team that played a whole season at 70%: the fewer the games, the further the cautious rate is marked down.

privacy.title: Privacy and terms
privacy.lede: This system keeps other people's replays and the Showdown names you say are yours. This page says how that data is stored and who can read it, and how to have it removed.

stored.title: What is stored
stored.account: Your own Google account, and no other way in.
stored.names: The Showdown names you add. Kept as you typed them, compared with case and punctuation removed.
stored.battles: One entry per replay you import, holding what was worked out from it: the format, when it was played, the result, the ratings, both teams, the turn count, and the opponent's name, their six, and which of them appeared.
stored.logs: The raw record of every replay you import, compressed and untouched, in storage only you can read.

access.title: Who can read it
access.body: You. What is stored is kept apart by account.

unverified.title: What this system cannot verify
unverified.body: A Showdown account gives other sites no way to confirm it, and there is no sign-in to use. So the same name may be on more than one person's list, and a name on your list grants nothing beyond deciding which of the battles you imported are treated as “your own”.
unverified.public: The replays themselves are public on Showdown to begin with, and both players' names and teams are there at the public address. Importing one copies that public record into your account. It does not make anything visible that was not already.

unbinding.title: When a name is removed
unbinding.body: Remove one of the names and every battle under it goes back to being a spectated battle: out of every statistic, off the page, still stored. Nothing is deleted, and adding the name again brings those battles back exactly as they were.

deletion.title: Deleting your data
deletion.body: There is no delete button yet. To have the account, your data and the stored records deleted, write to the author at the address below.

terms.title: Terms
terms.body: This is offered as is, with no warranty and no promise that it will keep running, keep your data, or be correct. It is not a backup: the replays it reads are Showdown's, at their own public addresses.
terms.trademarks: Not affiliated with Nintendo, Creatures, GAME FREAK, The Pokémon Company, Smogon or Pokémon Showdown. Pokémon names and sprites belong to their owners; replays belong to the people who played them.

notFound.title: There is nothing at this address
notFound.body: The link may be an old one, or the address may have a typo in it. Everything else is still here.

unexpected.title: Something went wrong here
unexpected.body: This page could not be shown. Loading it again is often enough; if it is not, nothing you have imported is affected.

login.title: Sign in
login.tagline: Google only. There is no password to forget.
login.failed: That sign-in did not go through.

import.title: Import a replay
import.tagline: Paste replay links, or sync everything a Showdown account has played.

paste.title: Paste links
paste.tagline: One replay per line. A private replay keeps its password in the address, so paste the whole thing.

import.label: Replay links, one per line

sync.title: Sync an account
sync.tagline: Every public replay Showdown will admit to for this name. Anything already imported is skipped, so pressing this again after a stopped import will pick up where it left off.
sync.label: Showdown name
sync.unusable: That is not a Showdown name. It needs at least one letter or digit.
sync.truncated: Showdown ran out of search pages before this account ran out of replays, so this is not the whole history. A single search reaches about 5000 replays, and the rest need a narrower search.

import.profileFailed: We could not read your Showdown names, so nothing can be imported right now: without them there is no way to tell which side of a battle is yours. Reload the page to try again.

progress.label: Import progress
progress.listing: Asking Showdown what this account has played…

import.badLink: That is not a Showdown replay link. Paste the address of the replay itself, like https://replay.pokemonshowdown.com/gen9championsvgc2026regmb-2667169457. A private replay keeps its password in the address, so paste that too.
import.unparsed: The raw record is stored, but this replay could not be read: {message} Nothing is lost. The battle is kept, and it can be read again once that record can be understood.

status.unparsedShort: stored, but could not be read

import.allSpectated: Every battle that came in was filed as one you only watched: no player in any of them is on your list of Showdown names, so none of them counts towards your statistics and none of them will show up. Add the name you played under and they become yours right away. The replays are already here and nothing needs importing again.

failed.notFound: Showdown has no replay at that link. It may have been deleted, or it may be private: a private replay is only served with the password its address carries.
failed.unavailable: Showdown did not answer. It may be down or rate limiting; wait a moment and import the link again.
failed.malformed: Showdown answered with something that is not a replay. Nothing was stored.
failed.storeFailed: The raw record could not be stored, so no battle was recorded. Nothing is half-imported, so try the link again.
failed.writeFailed: The raw record was stored, but the battle could not be written to your data. Import the link again.

battle.spectated: Neither player is on your list of Showdown names, so this battle is stored but counts towards none of your statistics and will not show up. Add the name you played under and it becomes yours right away. The replay is already here and nothing needs importing again.

aliases.title: Showdown names
aliases.tagline: Add every name you play under and they all count as the same you: after a rename, on an alt, on a separate account for a different format.
aliases.unverified: We cannot confirm that a Showdown account is yours, and neither can anyone else, because Showdown gives other sites no way to check. These names only decide which of the battles you import are treated as your own. They grant nothing, and the same name may be on more than one person's list.
aliases.label: Showdown name
aliases.empty: No names yet. Add the one you play under.
aliases.alreadyBound: {name} is already on your list. Names are compared without case or punctuation, so NotLittleStar and notlittlestar are the same name.
aliases.unusable: That is not a Showdown name. It needs at least one letter or digit.
aliases.loadFailed: We could not read your names, so nothing can be changed here right now. Reload the page to try again.
aliases.reattributeHint: Runs the names above over every battle you have imported. A run that changes nothing writes nothing, so there is nothing to undo.
aliases.removeBody: This takes {count} battle out of your statistics. It goes back to being a spectated battle, and binding the name again brings it back exactly as it was. | This takes {count} battles out of your statistics. They go back to being spectated battles, and binding the name again brings them back exactly as they were.
aliases.removeBodyUnknown: This takes every battle under that name out of your statistics. They go back to being spectated battles, and binding the name again brings them back exactly as they were.
aliases.unbound: Done: {count} battle went back to spectated. | Done: {count} battles went back to spectated.
aliases.reattributedWithReturned: Done: {attributed} battles are now yours, {reattributed} moved to a different name, and {unattributed} went back to spectated.
aliases.reattributed: Done: {attributed} battles are now yours, and {reattributed} moved to a different name.
aliases.reattributionFailed: That did not finish. {processed} battles were worked through before it stopped; nothing was undone, and running it again picks up the rest.

teams.title: Team performance
teams.noBrings: No game with this team has a complete bring yet.
teams.unfiled: These ended before all four had appeared, so no complete bring covers them. They count for the team and in none of the brings.
teams.notFound: No team here. It may have dropped out of the current filters.
teams.failed: Your battles could not be read. Try again in a moment.
teams.empty: No battles match these filters yet.
teams.emptyUnbound: None of the battles here are yours yet, and importing more will not change that. Which side of a battle is you is decided by the Showdown names in your settings, and there are none there, so every replay you import is filed as one you only watched. Add the name you play under first. The battles already imported under it become yours at the same moment, so nothing needs importing again.
teams.ranking: Cautious win rate {score}%, the sort key

trend.title: Recent form
trend.noRating: None of these battles carried a ladder score. A best-of series is not played on the ladder, so there is no number to plot.
trend.descriptive: This says what happened, not why.
trend.gap: The x axis is the calendar, so two months without a game take up two months of width and the win rate curve stretches flat across the break instead of hiding it. The score line does not stretch. It stops at the last battle that carried a score and starts again at the next one that did, because a best-of series is not played on the ladder and there is no number in between. Each point of the win rate curve covers the games leading up to that day, so the first points of a curve cover fewer games than the window says.
